sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Delaware, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 30Passed

To get a ballot by mail, your request must reach your county office by Friday, October 30, 2026; the law lets the office mail ballots no later than 4 days before the election. To apply and vote in person at your county office, the deadline is 12 noon on Monday, November 2, 2026 (the day before the election). (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your voted ballot must reach the Department of Elections office in your county by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026 (when the polls close). A postmark is not enough. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Sunday, November 1, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Delaware’s own site

At school away from home, in Delaware or in another state? What Delaware says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Yes, you need one of the reasons in state law to vote by absentee ballot. They include: working for the U.S. or Delaware government, or living outside the United States for a while (and your spouse or dependents with you); serving in the armed forces; your business or job keeps you away (this includes caring at home for a parent, spouse or child who needs constant care, and the state's application lists being a student under this reason); being sick or physically disabled; being away on vacation; your religion keeps you from voting at that time or on that day; or federal law lets you vote absentee. You check your reason on the application and sign it under penalty of perjury. (the law)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Go to the state's voter portal, iVote, look up your voter record and choose "Request an Absentee Ballot". Online requests arrive right away. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Download and fill in the absentee ballot application, sign it, and send it to the Department of Elections office in your county (New Castle, Kent or Sussex). You can also call your county office and ask them to mail you one. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Go to the Department of Elections office in your county, show proof of who you are and where you live, fill out and sign an application, and vote there. You can do this on normal business days from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., and up to 12 noon on the day before the election. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it to the Department of Elections office in your county. Postage is paid if you mail it in the U.S. or at an APO, FPO or DPO. (official page)
  • In person. Take it, or have someone take it, to the Department of Elections office in your county by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Absentee ballots cannot be turned in at early voting sites or polling places. (official page)

What the envelope needs

No witness or notary is needed. Put your marked ballot in the BALLOT ENVELOPE, then sign and date the oath on the back of the envelope and seal it. The application itself asks for your date of birth and signature; the last four digits of your Social Security number are optional. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Delaware’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Thursday, October 22, 2026 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Early voting for the general election runs from Thursday, October 22 through Sunday, November 1, 2026, at early voting sites in each county (none on Sunday, October 25). Hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. through October 27, then 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. from October 28 to November 1. State law lets any registered voter vote in person at these sites; no reason is asked. (official page)

Students

At school in Delaware, away from home

The Department of Elections says college students who are Delaware residents follow the same absentee process as everyone else. If you are registered in Delaware and cannot vote at your polling place on Election Day, send in your absentee ballot application as soon as you know your fall semester address; the application lists "student" as one of the reasons. The application asks for your Delaware address and, separately, the address to send the ballot to. (official page)

At school in another state, with Delaware as home

The same page applies to Delaware residents at college in another state: apply for an absentee ballot, giving your school address as the mailing address, and mail the ballot back so it reaches your county office by 8 p.m. on Election Day. The Department advises applying early and returning the ballot as soon as possible. The state's pages do not say more about where a student's home is; state law asks that a voter be a real ("bona fide") resident of Delaware. (official page)

Military and overseas

Members of the uniformed services, their families, and U.S. citizens living outside the United States use the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA), through iVote or on paper, sent to the county office by mail, fax or email no later than the third Monday before the election (Monday, October 19, 2026, which has passed). It is good through the next general election, and you can ask on it to be a permanent absentee voter. You can choose to get your ballot by email or fax. If your ballot does not come, you can use the Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot. The state's single contact is in the New Castle County office, (302) 577-5066. (official page)

Delaware in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Delaware requires a reason to vote absentee; early voting in person needs no reason.
  • If you asked for an absentee ballot and now want to vote at your polling place, the Department says to contact your county office before Election Day to cancel it; at the polls, you can vote if your absentee ballot has not been returned.
  • Some voters (sick or disabled, military and overseas, and caregivers) can ask to be permanent absentee voters and get a ballot for every election. The Department's page says permanent absentee voting was affirmed by the Delaware Supreme Court; we could not read that notice page.
  • Sick or disabled voters can ask for the ballot by email or fax in a form that works with accessibility software.
  • School board elections use a different absentee form.
  • The students_out_of_state text's last sentence draws on state law (source 7), not the student page.
  • The early voting eligibility sentence comes from state law 5402 (source 8); the dates and hours from the 2026 calendar (source 4).
  • That absentee ballots cannot be turned in at early voting sites or polling places comes from the Department's Ways to Vote page (source 9). The students_in_state sentence about the application's two addresses comes from the application form (source 2).

How this was checked

  • The FVAP page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.
